title: Working with images
idea: Image commands build, name, list and remove images. One image can carry several `name:tag` labels, such as `1.0` and `latest`, and keeps one ID.
points: `docker build -t bookstore-api:1.0 .` builds the Dockerfile in this folder into an image.
`docker pull node:20-alpine` downloads an image from Docker Hub, a public registry, without building.
`docker tag` gives an existing image another name. Nothing is copied.
`docker rmi` removes one name; the image goes with its last name.

hero.caption: `1.0` and `latest` are two names for one image. Delete one name and the image stays.

code.caption: Build an image, give it a second name, inspect it, then clean up.

walk.text: Build from the folder `.` (the build context). Name the image `bookstore-api:1.0`.
Add the name `latest` to the image you just built.
List the `bookstore-api` images. Both tags show the same image ID.
Show the image's layers, one row per layer, with the command that made each.
Download `node:20-alpine` from Docker Hub without building anything.
Remove the `latest` name. `1.0` still points at the image, so it stays.
Delete dangling images: untagged leftovers, often from rebuilding the same tag.

pitfalls: `latest` is only the default tag, not a promise of newest. Pin `20-alpine` or `1.0`.
Removing an image's last name fails while any container, even a stopped one, uses it.
Rebuilding a tag leaves the old image untagged; clear those with `docker image prune`.

quiz.q: You tagged bookstore-api:1.0 as latest, then ran docker rmi bookstore-api:latest. What happens?
options: Only the latest name goes; 1.0 and the image stay
Docker refuses: the image is in use
quiz.why: Both names point to one image. Removing a name leaves the image in place until its last name is gone.

takeaway: An image is its ID; tags are labels you add or remove.
